simple.meaning: סָמָר (çâmâr) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “bristling , i.e. shaggy.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 1 time across Jeremiah, beginning at Jeremiah 51:27. Its contexts include land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סָמָר (H5569).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.full: H5569. samar סָמָר adjective bristling, rough ; — ס ׳יֶלֶק Jer 51:27 bristling locust , perhaps with allusion to horn-like sheaths enclosing wings of the pupa, see Dr Joel and Amos, 58 (on formation compare Lag BN 50 ).
